# Chapter 4: Type Design Guidelines — 4–4.4

Rules that no analyzer enforces (judgment), and CONSIDER rules that analyzers only suggest. Open the examples file for the explanation and code the book gives with each rule.

## 4

- **FDG4001** DO ensure that each type is a well-defined set of related members, not just a random collection of unrelated functionality. — examples: examples/ch04-types-4-1-to-4-4.md#fdg4001

## 4.1 Types and Namespaces

- **FDG4002** DO use namespaces to organize types into a hierarchy of related feature areas. — examples: examples/ch04-types-4-1-to-4-4.md#fdg4002
- **FDG4003** AVOID very deep namespace hierarchies. Such hierarchies are difficult to browse because the user has to backtrack often.
- **FDG4004** AVOID having too many namespaces. — examples: examples/ch04-types-4-1-to-4-4.md#fdg4004
- **FDG4005** AVOID having types designed for advanced scenarios in the same namespace as types intended for common programming tasks. — examples: examples/ch04-types-4-1-to-4-4.md#fdg4005

## 4.2 Choosing Between Class and Struct

- **FDG4007** CONSIDER defining a struct instead of a class if instances of the type are small and commonly short-lived or are commonly embedded in other objects, especially arrays.
- **FDG4008** AVOID defining a struct unless the type has all of the following characteristics: — examples: examples/ch04-types-4-1-to-4-4.md#fdg4008

## 4.3 Choosing Between Class and Interface

- **FDG4009** DO favor defining classes over interfaces. — examples: examples/ch04-types-4-1-to-4-4.md#fdg4009
- **FDG4010** DO use abstract classes instead of interfaces to decouple the contract from implementations. — examples: examples/ch04-types-4-1-to-4-4.md#fdg4010
- **FDG4011** DO define an interface if you need to provide a polymorphic hierarchy of value types. — examples: examples/ch04-types-4-1-to-4-4.md#fdg4011
- **FDG4012** CONSIDER defining interfaces to achieve a similar effect to that of multiple inheritance. — examples: examples/ch04-types-4-1-to-4-4.md#fdg4012

## 4.4 Abstract Class Design

- **FDG4015** DO provide at least one concrete type that inherits from each abstract class that you ship. — examples: examples/ch04-types-4-1-to-4-4.md#fdg4015
